title: PII encoding & boundary hacks (personal lab notes)
content:
Quick personal lab notebook — capture weird PII encoding and boundary cases we keep seeing. Use this to prototype heuristics and small curated testset. Not for prod rules yet, just experiments and things to share with annotators.

Context / high level:
- Problem: PII detection/labeling pipeline misses or overlabels when strings include unusual unicode, obfuscation, or tokenizers split spans in unexpected places.
- Goal: create a compact set of heuristics + test examples that reduce false negatives (missed PII) and false positives (overzealous redaction) for phone/email/SSN-like and name detection.
- Constraints: keep runtime cost low (regex + token-aware heuristics), minimal ML reruns. Rules must be reversible or auditable.

Observed failure modes (real examples):
1) Zero-width and combining char obfuscation
   - "john​john@example.com" (ZWJ/ZWNJ/ZWSP inserted) -> current regex misses.
   - "Ñ̃Martinez" (N + combining tilde) -> tokenizer splits name into 2 tokens -> span broken.
2) Emoji + punctuation inside email local parts
   - "name🔥@example.com" sometimes flagged as invalid and skipped. But product wants to catch as PII.
3) Bracketed / obfuscated email forms that annotators should catch
   - "alice [at] example [dot] com" or "bob(at)example.com" -> semistructured obfuscation.
4) International phone formats + thin spaces
   - "+1
415A555A0199" (non-breaking thin spaces) -> split across tokens; naive digit-run heuristics fail.
5) Mixed-script substitution (cyrillic 'а' vs latin 'a')
   - "mаil@example.com" (the second char is Cyrillic small A) -> passing through normalization might convert or it might look unique and escape pattern.
6) Short numeric identifiers that look like SSN but are part of product codes -> overlabeling ("SKU 123-45-678")

Quick rules proposals (experimental):
- Pre-normalization layer (candidate-only):
  1) NFC normalize all strings for matching phase, but keep original text for final span output and audit. Note: combining characters -> unify.
  2) Remove/injectible chars: strip ZWJ/ZWNJ/ZWSP/BOM from matching pipeline but annotate if present (we may want to log obfuscation attempts).
  3) Unicode homoglyph detection: run cheap mapping of common homoglyphs (cyrillic a/e/o, greek etc) to latin for PII matching only; don't mutate saved text. Flagged when mapping applied.

- Regex/heuristic layer:
  1) Flexible email regex that tolerates emojis and single non-whitespace punctuation in local part (but limit length). Also accept obfuscated forms: replace common tokens like "[at]","(at)"," at "," dot ","[dot]" etc before running main regex.
  2) Phone detection: collapse all unicode spaces and punctuation into canonical digits+sep then match international pattern; accept leading "+" and country codes. If digits >= 7 and <= 15 -> candidate.
  3) Name spans: prefer longer contiguous alpha runs; if tokenizer splits due to combining marks, use char-level join to recompute contiguous alpha spans.
  4) Negative heuristics: if candidate sits inside a known product-code pattern (prefixes like SKU, ASIN, PROD_) then lower confidence.

- Labeling guidelines for annotators (for manual review batches):
  - Mark original raw span as PII only if it directly exposes contact/unique identifier. If obfuscated (e.g., "name [at] domain"), still label as PII but add tag "obfuscated" so downstream knows it's likely intentional.
  - For ambiguous numeric clusters: annotate with reason: "looks_like_ssn" vs "part_of_code". Example: "123-45-678" in a line with "SKU" -> label with reason=product-code.
  - Preserve original substring in metadata. Do NOT rewrite/remove ZWJ/ZWSP when saving human label.

Examples to include in curated tests (annotator instructions in parens):
1) "john​john@example.com"  (should be PII_EMAIL; note ZW char present)
2) "mаrk@domain.com" where the 'a' is Cyrillic (should be PII_EMAIL; mapping used)
3) "sally[at]work(dot)co" (PII_EMAIL, tag=obfuscated)
4) "+44 133 555 0199" (PII_PHONE, normalize spaces)
5) "Invoice: SKU 123-45-678 paid" (NOT PII_SSN, tag=product-code)
6) "Name: José́ Alvarez" (should be PII_NAME, combining char case)
7) "Contact: name🔥@example.com" (PII_EMAIL, allow emoji)
8) "Report for 2023-05-01: user id 555666" (NOT PII unless user id is known unique)

Edge marking conventions (for machine outputs):
- Output: span_start, span_end, label, confidence_bucket (high/med/low), canonicalized_value, flags (list)
- canonicalized_value: apply matching-normalization (strip zws, map homoglyphs, collapse spaces) but keep original saved separately.
- flags examples: ["obfuscated","unicode-mapped","zw-strip-applied"]

Pipeline cleanup quick steps (dev tasks):
- implement small preproc module that: NFC normalizes, strips ZW chars for matching, maps common homoglyphs. Unit tests for the examples above. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-configs/pull/221)
- Add a lightweight 'obfuscation detector' that looks for concrete indicators: tokens like "[at]" or broken digit runs with non-digit insertions -> raise obfuscation flag.
- Annotator QA batch: 200 samples with a focus on unicode/emoji/obfuscation (aim for 70% overlap between annotators for calibration).

Acceptance test ideas:
- Run detector on 1k random dataset where we know ground truth from support tickets. Measure FN reduction vs baseline and FP increase. Target: FN down 30% while FP increase < 5%.
- Log frequency of unicode-mapping events; if >1% of corpus, consider expanding homoglyph map or ML-based method.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which homoglyph table to use? Start tiny (cyrillic/greek to latin) and expand based on logs. Note: avoid Chinese/Kana mapping — too risky.
- How do we surface 'obfuscated' flag to downstream product? Probably as a metadata column; need PM input (ask @Maya).
- Annotator UX: should we highlight ZW characters? Might confuse some; instead show a warning line: "zero-width characters present".
- Performance checks: preproc must be sub-ms per document at scale. Need perf tests on 100k docs.

Notes to self:
- Share this with dataops and put 50 curated examples in the labeling tool as a calibration batch.
- Add a small doc for SRE explaining why normalized matching doesn't mutate stored content (audit + compliance).

References / links:
- quick regex draft in PR 221 (see linked_artifacts)
- slack thread around "ZW chars in emails" 2024-09-20

End of notebook. Will iterate after first annotator QA next week.
